summary.name: Flux
summary.one_liner: Flux is a browser-based AI hardware engineering tool that turns a product idea into a schematic, routed PCB, and fabrication-ready files.
use_cases: Designing a schematic and PCB from a plain-English description
Routing a board with AI, including differential pairs and power nets
Migrating an existing design from Altium, KiCad, Eagle or EasyEDA
Preparing Gerber, drill, BoM and pick-and-place files for manufacturing
Developing IoT, wearable, robotics or industrial electronics hardware
summary.what_it_does: Flux is an AI hardware engineer that generates schematics, places components, and routes multi-layer PCBs (up to eight layers) from a natural-language description. It reads component datasheets to ground part choices and runs continuous electrical and design rule checks. Users can ask it in chat to change trace widths, layers, or matched lengths while keeping manual control of routes. It imports projects from many ECAD tools and exports Gerbers, drill files, BoM, pick-and-place, and netlists. The tool runs in the browser with real-time collaboration.
notable: Runs entirely in the browser with no install and real-time collaboration
Imports projects from Altium, KiCad, Eagle, OrCAD, EasyEDA, SOLIDWORKS PCB and others
Reads datasheets to ground part decisions and runs continuous ERC/DRC checks
Encrypts data in transit and at rest; SOC 2-aligned cloud with SSO
caveats: Individual plans include a free trial; trial length and prices depend on the current offer
New Teams subscriptions start paid; Enterprise pricing is on request
Multi-layer PCB support is capped at eight layers
